questions.sentence: The cake ___ made by my grandmother.
questions.grammar_rule: Passive Voice: be + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Majhul nisbat: be + past participle
questions.explanation: Past Passive uses 'was/were + past participle'

questions.grammar_rule: Present Simple Passive: is/am/are + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Present Simple Passive: is/am/are + past participle
questions.explanation: Present Passive with singular subject uses 'is + past participle'

questions.correct_answer: The letter was written by John.
options: The letter was written by John.
questions.grammar_rule: Passive focuses on the action/object, not the doer
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Majhul nisbat harakatga/ob'ektga e'tibor qaratadi, bajaruvchiga emas
questions.explanation: Passive: Object + be + past participle (+ by agent)

questions.grammar_rule: Active to Passive: Object → Subject + be + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Aktiv → Passiv: Ob'ekt → Ega + be + past participle
questions.explanation: 'Spanish' (object) becomes subject; 'speak' → 'is spoken'

questions.sentence: The house ___ being built when we visited.
questions.grammar_rule: Past Continuous Passive: was/were being + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Past Continuous Passive: was/were being + past participle
questions.explanation: Past Continuous Passive shows an ongoing action in the past

questions.sentence: The book was wrote by Shakespeare.
questions.correct_answer: The book was written by Shakespeare.
questions.grammar_rule: Passive requires past PARTICIPLE, not past simple
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Majhul nisbatda past PARTICIPLE kerak, past simple emas
questions.explanation: Use 'written' (past participle), not 'wrote' (past simple)

questions.grammar_rule: Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle
questions.explanation: 'Already' indicates Present Perfect; passive form = has been + pp

questions.sentence: The project will ___ by next week.
questions.grammar_rule: Future Simple Passive: will be + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Future Simple Passive: will be + past participle
questions.explanation: Future Passive: will + be + past participle

hints: Present Perfect → has/have been + past participle
questions.grammar_rule: Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle
questions.explanation: 'Someone' (unknown) can be omitted; 'has stolen' → 'has been stolen'

questions.sentence: The documents ___ being reviewed at the moment.
questions.grammar_rule: Present Continuous Passive: is/am/are being + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Present Continuous Passive: is/am/are being + past participle
questions.explanation: 'At the moment' = ongoing action; plural 'documents' = 'are being'

questions.sentence: The house has been building for two years.
questions.correct_answer: The house has been being built for two years.
questions.grammar_rule: Present Perfect Continuous Passive: has been being + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Present Perfect Continuous Passive: has been being + past participle
questions.explanation: For ongoing action with duration, use 'has been being + past participle'

questions.sentence: The report ___ have been submitted yesterday.
questions.grammar_rule: Modal + have been + past participle for past passive with modals
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Modal + have been + past participle o'tmish majhul modal bilan
questions.explanation: Modal passive about past: modal + have been + past participle

questions.original_sentence: They are going to build a new hospital.
questions.correct_answer: A new hospital is going to be built.
hints: be going to + be + past participle
questions.grammar_rule: Future with 'going to' Passive: is/am/are going to be + pp
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Going to' kelajak majhul: is/am/are going to be + pp
questions.explanation: 'Going to' future passive: is going to be + past participle

questions.grammar_rule: Passive with reporting verbs: Subject + is said/believed + to + verb
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Xabar fe'llari bilan majhul: Ega + is said/believed + to + fe'l
questions.explanation: Reporting verb passive: 'He is believed to be' = 'People believe he is'

questions.sentence: The decision is thought ___ made too hastily.
questions.grammar_rule: Passive reporting verb + to have been + pp for past reference
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Majhul xabar fe'li + to have been + pp o'tmish uchun
questions.explanation: 'To have been + pp' refers to a completed past action in passive reporting

questions.sentence: The window was broken by accident.
questions.correct_answer: The window was broken by accident.
questions.grammar_rule: 'By' can indicate agent OR means/instrument
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'By' bajaruvchi YOKI vosita/usulni bildirishi mumkin
questions.explanation: This is correct! 'By accident' (manner) is different from 'by someone' (agent)

questions.instruction: Change to passive using 'have something done'
questions.original_sentence: She will ask someone to repair her car.
questions.correct_answer: She will have her car repaired.
questions.grammar_rule: Causative: have/get + object + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Sababli majhul: have/get + ob'ekt + past participle
questions.explanation: 'Have something done' = arrange for someone to do something for you

questions.grammar_rule: Causative past: had + object + past participle
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Sababli o'tgan zamon: had + ob'ekt + past participle
questions.explanation: 'Had something done' = someone did it for me (past)

questions.sentence: The criminal is said ___ escaped from prison.
questions.grammar_rule: Passive reporting + to have + past participle for past events
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Majhul xabar + to have + past participle o'tgan voqealar uchun
questions.explanation: 'Is said to have escaped' = People say he escaped (past)

questions.instruction: Change to passive with 'it' as subject
questions.original_sentence: People believe that he is a genius.
questions.correct_answer: It is believed that he is a genius.
hints: It + passive reporting verb + that clause
Or: He is believed to be...
questions.grammar_rule: Impersonal passive: It + is said/believed + that clause
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Noshaxsiy majhul: It + is said/believed + that gapi
questions.explanation: 'It is believed that...' is formal impersonal passive construction
